book_title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps
question: Does $294.84 leave a real margin of safety once we strip out 2026 Hormuz shipping spikes and price in $24.14 billion of debt?

epigraph.quote: Favorable pricing and regional spreads that boosted 2026 results may not recur once transit disruptions ease and new global liquefaction enters service.
epigraph.author: Cheniere Q3 2026 Risk & Outlook Synthesis [31][35]

web_blocks.title: 7.1 Headline Multiples vs. Normalized Post-Hormuz Earning Power

web_blocks.html: At the November 20, 2026 close of $294.84, Cheniere holds a $60.21 billion market cap and an $89.87 billion enterprise value [38][39]. On Finviz headline multiples, shares look cheap at 9.54x EV/EBITDA, 13.31x forward P/E, and 15.90x P/FCF [39]. That surface discount disappears once you examine the 2026 earnings mix. Raised FY2026 guidance of $9.00 billion Adjusted EBITDA ($8.75B–$9.25B) and $6.30 billion DCF ($6.05B–$6.55B) leans heavily on windfall spot margins [3][31].

In the first nine months of 2026, short-term marketing (CMI) volumes surged +73.4% YoY to 352 TBtu ($5,082 million) [31]. That spike tracked Strait of Hormuz disruptions that lifted European TTF from $11.27/MMBtu in February to $28.51/MMBtu in October and Asian JKM to $28.59/MMBtu [35]. Meanwhile, EIA expects U.S. LNG exports to climb +25.8% from 15.1 Bcf/d in 2025 to 19.0 Bcf/d in 2027 as Venture Global Plaquemines (27.2 mtpa), CP2 (29.0 mtpa), and Golden Pass ramp [35][36]. Stripping out the Hormuz spike puts normalized 2027E Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA near $7.30 billion across Cheniere's 56–58 million tonne plan [8][31].

web_blocks.takeaway: At $294.84, Cheniere's $89.87 billion enterprise value equals 12.31x normalized 2027E EBITDA ($7.30B) rather than 9.54x trailing EBITDA. Its 5.31% normalized net FCF yield sits just 27 bps above the 5.04% U.S. 10-year Treasury yield, leaving almost no margin of safety.

web_blocks.title: 7.2 Reverse DCF, Balance-Sheet Bridge & Cost of Equity Check

web_blocks.html: Our Reverse DCF starts from the November 19, 2026 rate backdrop: a 5.04% 10-year U.S. Treasury yield and a 4.76% 2-year yield [42]. Using a 4.54% equity risk premium and a 0.85 leverage-adjusted beta gives an 8.90% cost of equity. We reject Finviz's 0.07 trailing beta because Cheniere carries $24.138 billion of Q3 gross debt, a -$523 million working-capital deficit (0.90x current ratio), and an $11.76 billion 2027–2030 maturity wall [2][31][39].

On November 17, 2026, Cheniere closed $1.2 billion of 5.800% parent Senior Notes due 2037 at 99.313% of par [32]. Those funds refinance or bridge CCH's 5.125% 2027 secured notes at a +67.5 bps higher coupon while moving debt to the unsecured parent [32][37]. June 2026 NPNS accounting also freezes $349 million of net IPM value for non-linear COGS amortization (+$100M in 2027, +$101M in 2028) [31]. Modeling net parent FCF of $3.20B (2027E), $3.75B (2028E), and $4.25B (2029E), plus 2.5% terminal growth at 8.90% Ke, yields $63.88 billion equity value—$311.45/share today or $322.62/share 12 months forward on ~198 million post-buyback shares. Holding shares flat at today's 205.10 million diluted count yields a 50/50 blended fair value of $305.87/share (+3.74% vs. CMP), showing buyback dependency.

web_blocks.the_number: $315.00 normalized 12-month Base Case fair value (+6.84% vs. $294.84 CMP).
web_blocks.how_calculated: Blends 50% 10-year Parent Equity DCF ($322.62/sh forward at 8.90% Ke and 2.5% terminal growth) with 50% normalized 2027E EV/EBITDA at 12.5x ($91.25B EV less $22.48B net debt and $7.18B NCI = $61.59B, or $311.06/sh across 198.0M shares). On current 205.10M shares without buybacks, the 50/50 blend ($311.45 DCF + $300.29 EV/EBITDA) equals $305.87/sh (+3.74%).
web_blocks.the_inputs: CMP $294.84; 205.10M current shares and 198.0M forward shares; $24.138B Q3 gross debt and $1.663B cash ($22.475B net debt); $7.18B market-implied NCI; $7.30B normalized 2027E EBITDA; 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield.
web_blocks.the_range: Bear $195.00 (-33.86%) on 10.5x compressed $6.50B EBITDA; Base $315.00 (+6.84%); Bull $410.00 (+39.06%) if Hormuz spreads hold near $20/MMBtu ($8.80B EBITDA) and SPL Phase 1 reaches FID.
web_blocks.if_off: Every $0.50 billion swing in normalized 2027E EBITDA moves equity value by ~$31/share at 12.5x EV/EBITDA, while a +50 bps rise in cost of equity cuts DCF fair value by ~$18/share.

web_blocks.mechanism: A geopolitical supply shock spiked TTF above $50/MMBtu in 2022, lifting Cheniere's CMI marketing revenues and CFO to $10.523 billion before flows rerouted and LNG equities digested peak margins.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Cheniere's annual revenue fell 53.0% from $33.428 billion in FY2022 to $15.703 billion in FY2024, and CFO dropped 48.7% from $10.523 billion to $5.394 billion as European spreads normalized [12].
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: Geopolitical transit spikes create temporary cash windfalls that should pay down debt rather than being capitalized into permanent valuation multiples.

web_blocks.html: The peer table and 2022–2024 historical twin point to one clear verdict. Cheniere's reliability earns a premium over Venture Global (which faces arbitration and Stage 4 markdown) and integrated majors like Shell. Still, at 12.31x normalized 2027E EBITDA and $294.84, the market already prices in smooth Midscale 8&9 execution while ignoring 2027 spread compression.

Valuation Trigger: We would lift our $315.00 Base Case fair value toward $345.00+ only if Cheniere signs long-term SPAs at ≥$2.75/MMBtu for SPL Phase 1 with a funded FID. On price alone, a pullback to $258.00 yields just 6.07% normalized 2027E net parent FCF ($3.20B on ~$52.69B cap across 204.2M current shares, or 6.26% on 198.0M forward shares). Restoring a ≥7.0% normalized net FCF yield ($45.71B cap) requires a drop to ~$224.00/share ($223.86 on 204.2M current shares) or ~$231.00/share ($230.88 on 198.0M forward shares), paired with a fresh Stage 1/2 base and a new-base structural stop below that lower band (≤$206.00 at $224.00 for 5.06:1 R:R, or ≤$220.00 at $258.00 to clear ≥1.50:1 R:R to $315.00).

book_paragraphs: We completed our price-blind audit of Cheniere Energy across Chapters 1 through 6 and reached a clear qualitative view: this is a premier 56-million-tonne-per-year physical export franchise whose earnings quality is cyclical and conditional. Now we open the live market ledger for November 20, 2026, and ask what $294.84 per share asks us to believe.

On the surface, the headline screening numbers look tempting. At $294.84, Cheniere carries a $60.21 billion equity market cap and an $89.87 billion enterprise value. Finviz quotes the stock at 9.54 times trailing EBITDA, 13.31 times forward earnings, and 15.90 times trailing free cash flow. After a 51.67% year-to-date rally, you might see 9.54 times EBITDA and assume shares remain cheap.

That assumption fails once you apply our Pass 1 blind-spot findings. Why did 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance reach $9.00 billion and Distributable Cash Flow reach $6.30 billion? Because Strait of Hormuz tanker disruptions pushed TTF from $11.27 per MMBtu in February 2026 to $28.51 in October 2026, and JKM to $28.59. Cheniere's marketing arm boosted nine-month short-term sales by 73.4% to 352 TBtu and $5.082 billion. Management explicitly warned in the Q3 Form 10-Q that those spreads may not recur.

When we strip out the Hormuz spike and model Cheniere's 2027 plan of 56 to 58 million tonnes under normalized global spreads—as U.S. LNG exports climb 25.8% to 19.0 Bcf/d—normalized Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA settles near $7.30 billion. Subtract $1.18 billion of cash interest on $24.14 billion of gross debt, $1.02 billion of cash taxes and maintenance capex, and $1.05 billion attributable to CQP's 49.4% outside unitholders. That leaves $4.05 billion of normalized parent distributable cash flow, or $3.20 billion after $0.85 billion of Midscale 8 and 9 growth capex.

Compare that $3.20 billion of normalized net parent free cash flow against the $60.21 billion market cap. You get a 5.31% free cash flow yield while the 10-year U.S. Treasury pays a risk-free 5.04%. A 27-basis-point spread over Treasuries leaves almost no cushion for higher refinancing coupons like November's 5.800% 2037 notes or faster 2027 supply growth.

Our Reverse DCF and normalized multiple blend confirm that tightness. Discounting net parent cash flows at 8.90% cost of equity with 2.5% terminal growth yields $311.45 per share today and $322.62 twelve months forward. Valuing $7.30 billion of normalized EBITDA at 12.5 times—less $22.48 billion net debt and $7.18 billion NCI—yields $311.06 per share. Averaging both sets our unbiased 12-month Base Case fair value at $315.00, just 6.84% above today's close.

book_subsections.title: What the 2022–2024 Cycle Teaches About Peak LNG Spreads
paragraphs: We have Cheniere's own 2022 to 2024 filings as a direct guide to post-spike normalization. When Russian pipeline flows collapsed in 2022, Cheniere's revenue surged to $33.428 billion and operating cash flow hit $10.523 billion. By 2024, revenue fell 53% to $15.703 billion and operating cash flow settled at $5.394 billion.

Great infrastructure assets still face margin cycles on uncontracted spot cargoes. Paying 12.3 times normalized EBITDA after a 51.7% year-to-date rally leaves too little upside for a 5.04% interest-rate regime.

book_callouts.title: THE NORMALIZED YIELD SPREAD TEST
book_callouts.text: Never value a cyclical infrastructure stock on peak-disruption EBITDA. When 5.31% normalized net free cash flow yield barely clears the 5.04% 10-year Treasury yield, equity buyers are not paid for leverage or spread normalization.
